title: Spaces that are not word breaks give the edge dependence for free, but not its collapse at line breaks: the line, not the word, is the unit
statement: Measured on the practice evaluation layout (5,461 certain paragraph-token slots, letters as glyphs for the reference texts). Pinned Latin and Italian with their spaces removed and re-inserted by a fixed positional rule (a break after one of a set of letters with a fixed probability: after vowels at 0.5 or 0.35, after s m t n r l at 0.6, after vowels or m n s at 0.4; seed 1), so the spaces no longer mark words. Edge-glyph mutual information within lines: Latin 0.185 to 0.280, Italian 0.142 to 0.332, against the manuscript's 0.230 and Latin's 0.073 with its own spaces; so a writing in which spaces fall inside a continuous stream reproduces the cross-word edge dependence with no further mechanism. The same texts do not reproduce F-010: edge dependence within lines minus across line breaks (edge_mi_break) is -0.006 to 0.027 for Latin and -0.034 to 0.047 for Italian, against 0.173 for the manuscript, because the stream runs on from one line into the next. They also miss everything else: conditional glyph entropy 2.83 to 3.04 (manuscript 1.94), singletons 0.85 to 0.91 (0.71), one-glyph copies of recent words 0.006 to 0.015 (0.21). Answer to the step, for this family: re-spacing explains within-line edge dependence but not its discontinuity at line breaks; a single process that gives both must restart at each line, as the line-restarting chain of R-008 to R-017 does, so the line, not the word or the space-delimited token, behaves as the unit the text was composed in. The separator part of the question (certain against uncertain spaces) is not addressed. Practice split only.
check: Remove the spaces from a pinned reference text, re-insert them by the stated rules, pour into the practice evaluation layout and compute edge_mi, edge_mi_break, glyph_cond_entropy 2, hapax_share and near_copy (10, 4).
